chapters.title: Rational Conjugacy: Pochhammer Priors and Gamma Ratios
chapters.summary:
Pochhammer priors, introduced by Wang and Polson (2024), give conjugate inference for concentration parameters that enter a likelihood through ratios of Gamma functions with integer shifts. This chapter develops the theory around one principle, rational conjugacy: the Pochhammer family is not closed under updating, but proper rational densities on the positive half line are, and on that class every normalizing constant, moment and predictive probability is a finite sum of residues. It proves a residue formula with poles of any multiplicity, a closed form Mellin transform, an exact tail index, and a corrected reading of a Kullback Leibler risk bound: every member attains the rate N to the minus one times log N, and the half horseshoe only gives the smaller constant. A completely monotone representation identifies the half horseshoe on structural grounds and gives an exact latent variable sampler for Negative Binomial dispersion. An exponentially tilted family has a normalizer that is a finite sum of exponential integrals. The chapter locates the boundary of the method, gives a Zipf tail theorem, and quantifies the loss of digits in the residue expansion. Running examples are the Ewens concentration parameter and Corbet's butterflies.

#### From the literature

Pochhammer priors are Wang and Polson (2024). The Cesaro risk bound for horseshoe type priors is Polson and Scott (2011). The reciprocal gamma mixtures are He, Polson and Xu (2019). Damsleth (1975) gave the conjugate class for the two parameter Gamma. The chapter states which of these results it corrects.

#### New results

- [Residue formula for the normalizing constant of a rational density](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#normalizing_constant) (Theorem 9.3, page 346; proved): The integral of a rational function with poles of any multiplicity in the cut plane is a finite sum of residues times logarithms and powers. New in this book.
- [Mellin transform of a Pochhammer density](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#mellin_transform) (Theorem 9.6, page 347; proved): The Mellin transform of a Pochhammer density has a closed form on its maximal strip, which gives fractional and negative moments and the expected log. New in this book.
- [Shrinkage rate of the half horseshoe, corrected](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#shrinkage_rate_corrected) (Corollary 9.8, page 348; proved): Every Pochhammer prior attains the Kullback Leibler rate N^{-1} log N, and the half horseshoe only gives the smaller constant, which corrects the reading of the earlier bound. Corrects a statement of Wang and Polson (2024), Pochhammer priors for sparse count models, arXiv:2402.09583.
- [Exact tail index of the Pochhammer law](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#exact_tail_index_of_the_pochhammer_law) (Corollary 9.7, page 348; proved): The Pochhammer density is regularly varying with an exact tail index given by its parameters, so it has power law tails and finitely many moments. New in this book.
- [Conditional exponentiality of the half horseshoe](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#conditional_exponentiality) (Theorem 9.9, page 348; proved): A Pochhammer density is completely monotone exactly when m and d are zero, in which case it is a scale mixture of exponentials, which yields an exact latent variable sampler. New in this book.
- [Tilted normalizer with exponential integrals](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#tilted_normalizer) (Theorem 9.16, page 353; proved): Exponentially tilting a rational density gives a normalizer that is a finite sum of exponential integrals, valid for every degree of the numerator. New in this book.
- [Exact dispersion block for Negative Binomial regression](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#exact_dispersion_block) (Proposition 9.21, page 358; proved): The dispersion parameter of Negative Binomial regression with a Pochhammer prior has an exact conditional law, so a partially collapsed Gibbs sampler needs no Metropolis step. New in this book.
- [Zipf tails of the Negative Binomial Beta Pochhammer hierarchy](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#zipf_tails) (Theorem 9.20, page 358; proved): The marginal law of the counts in the hierarchy has an exact power law tail with a logarithmic correction, so a Zipf exponent can be set as a prior hyperparameter. New in this book.
- [Boundary Zipf law of the Yule Simon prior predictive](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#boundary_zipf_law) (Proposition 9.22, page 363; proved): Under a Pochhammer prior on the Zipf exponent the Yule Simon prior predictive is proper but has no positive moments. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Pochhammer prior, rational conjugacy, residue calculus, Mellin transform, half horseshoe, completely monotone, concentration parameter, Negative Binomial regression, dispersion, Zipf law, Yule Simon distribution, exponential integral, Dirichlet process, Pitman Yor, Kullback Leibler risk, Corbet butterflies

chapters.title: Sufficiency Without a Likelihood in Population Genetics
chapters.summary:
Approximate Bayesian computation was invented in population genetics because coalescent likelihoods are intractable, and it has two defects: the analyst chooses summary statistics, so the object computed is the posterior given the summary and not the posterior given the data, and the analyst chooses a tolerance. This chapter replaces the apparatus with a learned transport map. By noise outsourcing the posterior is a deterministic function of the data and an independent uniform, and that function is the population minimiser of an expected check loss, so a regression with a quantile network can fit it. The central theorem is that a map factoring through a bottleneck summary and attaining the Bayes risk makes the summary sufficient, so sufficiency becomes a test on risks; a converse and a bound by the Wasserstein distance between the posterior and its summary based version complete the picture. The chapter treats Ewens's sufficiency of the number of alleles and proves that Watterson's number of segregating sites is not sufficient for the mutation rate. Experiments report learned posteriors against exact ones, including a repair of location scale structure that works in some seeds and fails in others.

#### From the literature

Rejection approximate Bayesian computation in genetics is due to Tavare and coauthors (1997) and Beaumont and coauthors (2002). Noise outsourcing is a standard lemma. The check loss is the loss of quantile regression. Ewens (1972) showed that the number of alleles is sufficient for theta. Watterson (1975) is the source of the segregating sites statistic.

#### New results

- [The check loss identifies the posterior](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#the_check_loss_identifies_the_posterior) (Theorem 10.8, page 394; proved): Minimizing the expected check loss over maps of a uniform variable and the data recovers the posterior quantile function exactly. New in this book.
- [A bottleneck that attains the Bayes risk is sufficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#a_bottleneck_that_attains_the_bayes_risk_is_sufficient) (Theorem 10.12, page 399; proved): If a learned map that factors through a summary of the data attains the minimal check loss, the summary is sufficient, so sufficiency can be tested by comparing risks. New in this book.
- [Excess risk is a posterior distance](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#excess_risk_is_a_posterior_distance) (Theorem 10.16, page 402; proved): The extra check loss of a summary based map is sandwiched between multiples of the expected squared Wasserstein distance between the posterior and its summary based version. New in this book.
- [Converse of the bottleneck sufficiency theorem](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#converse) (Proposition 10.21, page 404; proved): A Bayes sufficient statistic always admits a map through it that attains the minimal risk. New in this book.
- [The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#suff_prop_notsuff) (Proposition 10.25, page 412; proved): Given a single segregating site, the chance that it is carried by n minus 1 sequences changes with theta, so the count of sites is not sufficient. New in this book.

#### Key terms

approximate Bayesian computation, likelihood free inference, sufficiency, Bayes sufficiency, noise outsourcing, check loss, quantile regression, quantile neural network, Wasserstein distance, generative Bayesian computation, Ewens sampling formula, segregating sites, Watterson, site frequency spectrum

chapters.title: Learning to Coalesce
chapters.summary:
Kingman's coalescent is the historical home of likelihood free inference: simulation is trivial and likelihood evaluation is not. This chapter studies generative Bayesian computation for it. Under the infinite sites model the number of segregating sites is a sum of independent geometric variables, one per level of the coalescent, which gives Watterson's mean and variance, an exactly computable likelihood for the site count, and a Bernoulli geometric duality with the Ewens block count. The haplotype partition has the Ewens law, and all these statistics carry Fisher information of order the log of the sample size over theta. The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta, shown by an explicit calculation for three and four sequences, so a summary must be learned and not derived. A ceiling is proved: any DeepSets encoder built from per site permutation invariant features factors through the site frequency spectrum, a strict coarsening of the maximal invariant, and the haplotype count escapes that ceiling. Experiments with n equal to 30 compare learned posteriors with an exact posterior given S, including a growth model, and simulation based calibration shows residual miscalibration of the learned maps.

#### From the literature

Kingman's coalescent is Kingman (1982). The geometric structure of segregating sites is implicit in Watterson (1975). The Feller coupling is classical. Likelihood free inference for the coalescent starts with Tavare and coauthors (1997) and Beaumont and coauthors (2002). DeepSets encoders are due to Zaheer and coauthors.

#### New results

- [Bernoulli geometric duality between the Ewens block count and segregating sites](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#bernoulli_geometric_duality) (Corollary 11.7, page 439; proved): The number of blocks of the Ewens sampling formula has the same law as one plus the number of coalescent levels that carry at least one mutation. New in this book.
- [The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta, likelihood argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#is_not_sufficient_for) (Proposition 11.12, page 443; proved): The conditional law of the infinite sites data given the site count depends on theta through the latent tree, shown explicitly for three and four sequences. New in this book.
- [DeepSets encoders factor through the site frequency spectrum](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#deepsets_encoders_factor_through_the_spectrum) (Theorem 11.16, page 445; proved): Any encoder built from per site permutation invariant features depends on the data only through the site frequency spectrum, which caps what such an encoder can learn. New in this book.
- [The spectrum is a strict coarsening of the gene tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#spectrum_is_a_strict_coarsening) (Corollary 11.17, page 445; proved): The site frequency spectrum is strictly coarser than the gene tree, which is the maximal invariant, so no per site DeepSets encoder can recover what the spectrum loses. New in this book.
- [The haplotype count escapes the site frequency spectrum](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#haplotype_count_escapes_the_spectrum) (Proposition 11.18, page 446; proved): The haplotype count is invariant under relabelling of lineages and sites but is not a function of the site frequency spectrum. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Kingman coalescent, infinite sites model, segregating sites, Watterson estimator, geometric decomposition, Feller coupling, haplotype count, site frequency spectrum, DeepSets, permutation invariant encoder, generative Bayesian computation, simulation based calibration, demographic growth, likelihood free inference

chapters.title: Open Problems and the Future
chapters.summary:
This chapter collects the problems that the other chapters leave open, arranged by the three themes of the book: selection and the additive model, the sampling theory of neutral alleles, and inference without a likelihood. As many as possible are stated as precise mathematical or statistical questions, including one conjecture, that no sampling weight depending on atom index and position that charges every interval carries a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet law to a different one, which would make the rigidity theorem of the earlier chapter complete. The chapter then adds the larger questions that the genomic era forces on statistical genetics: samples comparable in size to the population, genealogies inferred at biobank scale, ancient DNA as a time series, the portability of polygenic prediction, and learned inference whose calibration has to be checked and not assumed. Short calculations show the scale of the difficulties: the slow approach of the singleton fraction to Pitman's discount parameter, the gap between marginal and conditional calibration, and the failure of the coalescent when the sample approaches the size of the population.

#### From the literature

The chapter draws on the results of the earlier chapters and on the literature they cite, in particular Pitman's discount parameter and the Ewens Pitman family.

#### New results

- [Conjecture, rigidity of Poisson Dirichlet under general ascertainment](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#future_conj_rigid) (Conjecture 12.7, page 467; open): No sampling weight depending on atom index and position that charges every interval is conjectured to carry a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet law to a different one. New in this book.

#### Key terms

open problems, conjecture, rigidity of Poisson Dirichlet, ascertainment, biobank scale genealogies, ancient DNA, polygenic prediction portability, calibration of learned posteriors, coalescent with large samples, singleton fraction

results.name: Moving projection lemma
results.summary: For arbitrary smooth genotype frequency paths the rate of change of mean Malthusian fitness is Fisher's additive term plus a remainder that pairs the least squares deviations with the logarithmic velocity of the genotype frequencies.
results.statement: Let $P_{uv}(t)$ be smooth genotype frequencies at a locus, with no assumption of Hardy Weinberg proportions, let $m_{uv}$ be fixed Malthusian fitnesses and $\bar m=\sum_{u,v}P_{uv}m_{uv}$. Let $A_{uv}=\beta_u+\beta_v$ be the fitted values of the $L^2(P(t))$ projection of $m$ onto the span of the gene contents, with average effects $\beta_u$, and let $\delta_{uv}=m_{uv}-A_{uv}$ be the residuals. Then $\frac{d\bar m}{dt}=\sum_{u,v}\dot P_{uv}A_{uv}+\sum_{u,v}\dot P_{uv}\delta_{uv}=\mathcal{A}+\mathcal{R}$, where $\mathcal{A}=2\sum_u\dot p_u\beta_u$ is Fisher's term, with $p_u$ the frequency of allele $u$, and, since $\sum_{u,v}P_{uv}\delta_{uv}=0$, the remainder is $\mathcal{R}=\sum_{u,v}\dot P_{uv}\delta_{uv}=\langle\delta,\dot P/P\rangle_t$.
results.label: ftns:lem:moving

results.name: Whole genome Fundamental Theorem decomposition
results.summary: For arbitrary genotype frequency paths, the rate of change of mean Malthusian fitness splits exactly into an additive part and a remainder; the remainder vanishes whenever the log frequencies move inside the span of the gene contents, and it vanishes for every assignment of fitnesses only then.
results.statement: Let $P_g(t)$ be genotype frequencies over a finite set of genotypes $g$, with no assumption of Hardy Weinberg proportions or of linkage equilibrium, let $m_g$ be the Malthusian fitness of genotype $g$, let $\bar m=\sum_g P_g m_g$, let $V$ be the span of the gene content functions (the additive functions of the genotype), let $\beta_{ij}$ be the whole genome average effects, defined as the coefficients of the $L^2(P_t)$ projection of $m$ onto $V$, let $\dot p_{ij}$ be the rates of change of the allele frequencies, and let $\delta=m-\Pi_t m$ be the residual of that projection. Then $\frac{d\bar m}{dt}=\mathcal{A}+\mathcal{R}$ with $\mathcal{A}=2\sum_{i,j}\dot p_{ij}\beta_{ij}$ and $\mathcal{R}=\sum_g\dot P_g\,\delta_g=\langle\delta,\partial_t\log P\rangle_t$. Moreover $\mathcal{R}=0$ whenever $\partial_t\log P\in V$, and if $\mathcal{R}=0$ for every assignment of Malthusian parameters $m$ then necessarily $\partial_t\log P\in V$.
results.label: ftns:thm:whole

results.name: Exponential family factorization of the remainder
results.summary: When the genotype distribution moves inside an exponential family whose main effects are the gene contents, the main effects contribute nothing to the remainder, which depends on the interaction coordinates alone.
results.statement: Let the genotype distribution move within the family $\log P_g(t)=\sum_jc_j(t)X_j(g)+\sum_A\theta_A(t)u_A(g)-\psi(c(t),\theta(t))$, where $\{X_j\}$ spans the space $V$ of gene contents and $\{u_A\}$ completes the basis, and let $\delta$ be the residual of the projection of fitness onto $V$ in $L^2(P_t)$. Then $\langle\delta,\partial\log P/\partial c_j\rangle_t=0$ for every main effect $j$, and $\mathcal{R}=\sum_A\langle\delta,u_A\rangle_t\,\dot\theta_A$. Here $\mathcal{R}=\sum_g\dot P_g\,\delta_g$ is the remainder in $d\bar m/dt=\mathcal{A}+\mathcal{R}$, with $\bar m$ the mean Malthusian fitness.
results.label: ftns:thm:expfam

results.name: Remainder in Lindley coordinates
results.summary: At a biallelic locus, in the coordinates of allele frequency and Hardy Weinberg disequilibrium, the remainder is the dominance contrast times the Fisher information times the velocity of the disequilibrium coefficient.
results.statement: At a biallelic locus with all three genotype classes present, parametrize the genotype simplex by $(p,\alpha)$, where $p$ is the frequency of the allele $A_1$ and $\alpha=\log\{4P_{11}P_{22}/P_{12}^2\}$ is Lindley's Hardy Weinberg disequilibrium coefficient. Let $m_{11},m_{12},m_{22}$ be the Malthusian fitnesses, $D=m_{11}-2m_{12}+m_{22}$, and $\mathcal{I}(\alpha)=(1/P_{11}+4/P_{12}+1/P_{22})^{-1}$ the Fisher information about $\alpha$ per genotyped individual. Then the remainder of the moving projection lemma, $\mathcal{R}=\sum_{u,v}\dot P_{uv}\delta_{uv}$ with $\delta$ the residual of the $L^2(P)$ projection of $m$ onto the gene contents, equals $D\,\mathcal{I}(\alpha)\dot\alpha$.
results.label: ftns:thm:lindley

results.name: The residual in closed form at a biallelic locus
results.summary: At a biallelic locus the residual of the additive projection is one known vector times one number, which gives the dominance variance and the remainder in closed form.
results.statement: At a biallelic locus let the genotypes $A_1A_1,A_1A_2,A_2A_2$ have frequencies $P_{11},P_{12},P_{22}$, all positive (all three genotype classes present), and Malthusian fitnesses $m_{11},m_{12},m_{22}$. Let $V$ be the span of the gene contents, let $\delta$ be the residual of the $L^2(P)$ projection of $m$ onto $V$, let $D=m_{11}-2m_{12}+m_{22}$, let $\alpha=\log\{4P_{11}P_{22}/P_{12}^2\}$ be Lindley's Hardy Weinberg disequilibrium coefficient, and let $\mathcal{I}(\alpha)=(1/P_{11}+4/P_{12}+1/P_{22})^{-1}$ be the Fisher information about $\alpha$ per genotyped individual. Write $\sigma^2_G=\sum_{u,v}P_{uv}(m_{uv}-\bar m)^2$ for the total genetic variance, $\sigma^2_D=\sum_{u,v}P_{uv}\delta_{uv}^2$ for the dominance variance and $\mathcal{A}$ for the additive variance. Let $h=(1/P_{11},\,-2/P_{12},\,1/P_{22})$. Then $h$ spans the orthogonal complement of $V$ in $L^2(P)$, and $\delta=D\,\mathcal{I}(\alpha)\,h$, $\sigma^2_D=D^2\mathcal{I}(\alpha)$ and $\mathcal{A}=\sigma^2_G-D^2\mathcal{I}(\alpha)$. For every velocity of the genotype frequencies, the remainder $\mathcal{R}=\langle\delta,\dot P/P\rangle_t$ equals $D\,\mathcal{I}(\alpha)\dot\alpha$. Under Hardy Weinberg proportions $\sigma_D^2=(pqD)^2$, the classical dominance variance $(2pqd)^2$ in the parametrization $m=(\mu+a,\mu+d,\mu-a)$ with $D=-2d$.
results.label: ftns:prop:resid

results.name: Two locus residual
results.summary: For two biallelic loci the residual is an interaction contrast times the information about linkage disequilibrium, so recombination alone changes mean fitness at an exact rate.
results.statement: For two biallelic loci let the haplotypes $AB,Ab,aB,ab$ have positive frequencies $x_1,\dots,x_4$ and Malthusian fitnesses $m_1,\dots,m_4$, let $n_A,n_B\in\{0,1\}$ be the gene contents and $V=\operatorname{span}\{1,n_A,n_B\}$, and let $\delta$ be the residual of the $L^2(x)$ projection of $m$ onto $V$. Define $\lambda=\log\{x_1x_4/(x_2x_3)\}$, the log odds ratio of the haplotype table, $E=m_1-m_2-m_3+m_4$, the interaction contrast of fitness, $\mathcal{I}(\lambda)=(\sum_i1/x_i)^{-1}$, the Fisher information about $\lambda$ per haplotype, and $D_{AB}=x_1x_4-x_2x_3$. Let $h=(1/x_1,-1/x_2,-1/x_3,1/x_4)$. Then $h\perp V$ in $L^2(x)$, and $\delta=E\,\mathcal{I}(\lambda)\,h$, $\sigma^2_{AB}=E^2\mathcal{I}(\lambda)$ where $\sigma^2_{AB}=\sum_ix_i\delta_i^2$ is the epistatic variance, and the remainder $\mathcal{R}=\sum_i\dot x_i\delta_i$ equals $E\,\mathcal{I}(\lambda)\dot\lambda$. In particular, recombination at rate $r$ in continuous time, $\dot x=-rD_{AB}(1,-1,-1,1)$, moves no allele frequency and changes mean fitness at the rate $\mathcal{R}=-rD_{AB}E$, exactly.
results.label: ftns:prop:twolocus

results.name: Exact remainder for one locus with k alleles
results.summary: In the one locus random mating model with constant fitnesses, the change in mean fitness is the additive term divided by mean fitness plus an explicit quadratic remainder in the dominance deviations.
results.statement: Consider discrete nonoverlapping generations, one locus with $k$ alleles, random mating and constant genotypic fitnesses $w_{ij}$, so that genotype frequencies are $p_ip_j$. Write $\bar w=\sum_{i,j}p_ip_jw_{ij}$, $w_{i\cdot}=\sum_jp_jw_{ij}$, $\alpha_i=w_{i\cdot}-\bar w$, $\Delta p_i=p_i\alpha_i/\bar w$, and $\delta_{ij}=w_{ij}-\bar w-\alpha_i-\alpha_j$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the additive term, $\mathcal{A}=2\sum_ip_i\alpha_i^2$. Then $\Delta\bar w=\frac{\mathcal{A}}{\bar w}+\frac{1}{\bar w^{2}}\sum_{i,j}\delta_{ij}(p_i\alpha_i)(p_j\alpha_j)$. With two alleles and $D=w_{11}-2w_{12}+w_{22}$ this is $\Delta\bar w=\mathcal{A}/\bar w+D(\Delta p)^2$.
results.label: ftns:thm:main

results.name: Exact relative error of the Fundamental Theorem, two alleles
results.summary: At a biallelic locus the relative size of the remainder against the additive term is exactly D pq divided by twice mean fitness, which is first order in the selection coefficient.
results.statement: At a biallelic locus under the conditions of the exact remainder theorem for one locus, with allele frequencies $p$ and $q=1-p$, mean fitness $\bar w$ and $D=w_{11}-2w_{12}+w_{22}$, the remainder $\mathcal{R}=D(\Delta p)^2$ satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}}{\mathcal{A}/\bar w}=\frac{D\,pq}{2\bar w}$.
results.label: ftns:cor:relerr

results.name: Bias of the plug in estimate of additive variance
results.summary: With orthogonal columns, the plug in estimator of the additive variance is inflated by the number of loci times the noise variance over the sample size.
results.statement: Let $y=X\alpha+\varepsilon$ with $n$ individuals and $L$ loci, with $\mathbb{E}\varepsilon=0$ and $\operatorname{Var}\varepsilon=\sigma_\varepsilon^2I_n$. Suppose the columns of $X$ are orthogonal, $x_\ell^\top x_m=0$ for $\ell\ne m$, with $x_\ell^\top x_\ell=nh_\ell$, and let $\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell=x_\ell^\top y/(x_\ell^\top x_\ell)$ and $\sigma_A^2=\sum_\ell h_\ell\alpha_\ell^2$. Then (a) $\mathbb{E}\big[\sum_\ell h_\ell(\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell)^2\big]=\sigma_A^2+L\sigma_\varepsilon^2/n$; (b) if in addition $\varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma_\varepsilon^2I_n)$, then $\operatorname{Var}\big[\sum_\ell h_\ell(\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell)^2\big]=4\sigma_\varepsilon^2\sigma_A^2/n+2L\sigma_\varepsilon^4/n^2$.
results.label: hs:prop:bias

results.name: Shrinkage is conservative
results.summary: Any shrinkage weights give an estimate of the additive variance no larger than the plug in estimate.
results.statement: Let $\hat\sigma^2_A(\kappa)=\sum_\ell h_\ell(1-\kappa_\ell)^2(\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell)^2$ be the additive variance computed from shrunken effects with shrinkage weights $\kappa_\ell$. For any $\kappa\in[0,1]^L$, $\hat\sigma_A^2(\kappa)\le\hat\sigma_A^2(0)=\sum_\ell h_\ell(\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell)^2$, with equality only if $\kappa_\ell=0$ whenever $\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell\ne0$.
results.label: hs:prop:conservative

results.name: Oracle shrinkage understates the additive variance
results.summary: Shrinkage tuned to estimate each average effect as well as possible necessarily understates the additive variance, by an explicit amount.
results.statement: Let $y=X\alpha+\varepsilon$ with $n$ individuals and $L$ loci, $\mathbb{E}\varepsilon=0$, $\operatorname{Var}\varepsilon=\sigma_\varepsilon^2I_n$, and orthogonal columns with $x_\ell^\top x_\ell=nh_\ell$. Let $\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell=x_\ell^\top y/(x_\ell^\top x_\ell)$, let $\hat\alpha_\ell=(1-\kappa_\ell)\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell$ be the shrunken effect, $\hat\sigma^2_A(\kappa)=\sum_\ell h_\ell(1-\kappa_\ell)^2(\hat\alpha^{\mathrm{marg}}_\ell)^2$ and $\sigma_A^2=\sum_\ell h_\ell\alpha_\ell^2$. Let $v_\ell=\sigma_\varepsilon^2/(nh_\ell)$ and let $\kappa^*_\ell=v_\ell/(\alpha_\ell^2+v_\ell)$ be the shrinkage weight minimizing $\mathbb{E}(\hat\alpha_\ell-\alpha_\ell)^2$. Then $\mathbb{E}[\hat\sigma_A^2(\kappa^*)]=\sum_\ell h_\ell\alpha_\ell^4/(\alpha_\ell^2+v_\ell)<\sigma_A^2$, with shortfall $\sum_\ell h_\ell\alpha_\ell^2v_\ell/(\alpha_\ell^2+v_\ell)$.
results.label: hs:prop:oracle

results.name: The coherent estimator is the posterior mean of the quadratic
results.summary: The posterior mean of the additive variance is the sum of the squared posterior means plus the posterior variances, so it is never below the plug in of the posterior means.
results.statement: Let $m_\ell=\mathbb{E}[\alpha_\ell\mid y]$ and $s_\ell^2=\operatorname{Var}(\alpha_\ell\mid y)$ under the horseshoe model of the chapter. Then $\mathbb{E}[\sigma_A^2\mid y]=\sum_\ell h_\ell(m_\ell^2+s_\ell^2)\ge\sum_\ell h_\ell m_\ell^2$, the last sum being the plug in of the posterior means.
results.label: hs:prop:posterior

results.name: Inflation of Fisher's fitted projection
results.summary: The unregularized fit of the projection that defines the average effects inflates the estimated additive variance by exactly the number of parameters times the noise variance over the sample size.
results.statement: Let $y=X\beta+\varepsilon$ with $X$ an $N\times p$ matrix of full column rank $p$, $\mathbb{E}\varepsilon=0$ and $\operatorname{Var}\varepsilon=\sigma^2I_N$, let $H$ be the orthogonal projection onto the column space of $X$, and let $\hat\sigma_A^2=\|Hy\|^2/N$ and $\sigma_A^2=\|X\beta\|^2/N$. Then $\mathbb{E}\hat\sigma_A^2=\sigma_A^2+p\sigma^2/N$.
results.label: mp:prop:optimism

results.name: Saturation of the optimism past the interpolation threshold
results.summary: The inflation of the fitted additive variance grows linearly in the number of parameters up to the sample size and is constant afterwards.
results.statement: Let $y=X\beta+\varepsilon$ with $X$ an $N\times p$ matrix, $\mathbb{E}\varepsilon=0$ and $\operatorname{Var}\varepsilon=\sigma^2I_N$, let $H$ be the orthogonal projection onto the column space of $X$, and let $\hat\sigma_A^2=\|Hy\|^2/N$ and $\sigma_A^2=\|X\beta\|^2/N$. When $H$ has rank $\min(p,N)$, as it does generically, $\mathbb{E}\hat\sigma_A^2=\sigma_A^2+\sigma^2\min(p,N)/N$, so the inflation grows linearly in $p$ up to $p=N$ and is constant at $\sigma^2$ thereafter.
results.label: mp:cor:saturate

results.name: Shrinkage weights are stick breaking weights
results.summary: The Beta law of the horseshoe type shrinkage weight is exactly the law of the first stick breaking weight of the two parameter GEM family, which links shrinkage priors to Ewens Pitman partitions.
results.statement: Let $\kappa\sim\mathrm{Beta}(a,b)$ with $a\in(0,1]$ and $b>0$. Then $\kappa$ has the law of the first stick breaking weight $W_1$ of $\mathrm{GEM}(\alpha,\theta)$ under $\alpha=1-a$ and $\theta=a+b-1$, and this map is a bijection from $\{a\in(0,1],\,b>0\}$ onto $\{0\le\alpha<1,\,\theta>-\alpha\}$.
results.label: mp:thm:main

results.name: Spectrum and shrinkage profile
results.summary: The mean intensity of the atoms of a random discrete distribution is the density of a size biased pick divided by x, which gives the expected allele frequency spectrum of a shrinkage prior from the density of its shrinkage weight.
results.statement:
Let $(P_i)$ be a random discrete distribution and let $
u$ be the mean intensity of its atoms, so that $\mathbb{E}\sum_ih(P_i)=\int_0^1h(x)
u(x)\,dx$ for bounded $h$ vanishing at the origin. Let $W$ be a size biased pick from $(P_i)$, with density $f_W$. Then $f_W(x)=x\,
u(x)$, equivalently $
u(x)=x^{-1}f_W(x)$. Consequently, for a global local prior whose shrinkage weight $\kappa\sim\mathrm{Beta}(a,b)$ with $a\in(0,1]$ and $b>0$ has density $f_\kappa$, matched by the stick breaking theorem so that $f_\kappa=f_W$ for the size biased pick of $\mathrm{PD}(1-a,a+b-1)$, the induced expected allele frequency spectrum in a sample of size $n$, with $a_j$ the number of alleles carried by exactly $j$ sequences, satisfies $\mathbb{E}\,a_j= inom{n}{j}\int_0^1x^{j-1}(1-x)^{n-j}f_\kappa(x)\,dx$.
results.label: mp:thm:spectrum

results.name: Discovery rates of shrinkage priors
results.summary: A global local prior with a Beta shrinkage weight discovers a number of signals that grows like a power of the sample size, n to the one half for the horseshoe, or only logarithmically when a equals one.
results.statement: Let a global local prior have shrinkage weight $\kappa\sim\mathrm{Beta}(a,b)$ with $a\in(0,1]$ and $b>0$, matched to $\mathrm{PD}(1-a,a+b-1)$ by the stick breaking theorem. The induced expected number of occupied blocks in a sample of size $n$ grows like $n^{1-a}$ when $a<1$ and like $(a+b-1)\log n=b\log n$ when $a=1$. In particular the horseshoe, with $a=1/2$, discovers of the order of $n^{1/2}$ signals, and every prior with $a=1$, that is the uniform shrinkage prior and the ridge like priors $\mathrm{Beta}(1,b)$, discovers of the order of $b\log n$.
results.label: mp:cor:growth

results.name: Effective model size of a shrinkage prior
results.summary: The expected number of coefficients that survive the penalty grows like a power of the sample size, or like a logarithm when a equals one, at the canonical global scale.
results.statement: Let $\kappa_\tau=1/(1+\tau^2\lambda^2)$ where $\lambda$ is such that $\kappa_1\sim\mathrm{Beta}(a,b)$ with $a\in(0,1]$ and $b>0$. Then as $\tau\downarrow0$, $\mathbb{E}(1-\kappa_\tau)\sim\frac{\pi}{B(a,b)\sin(\pi a)}\tau^{2a}$ for $0<a<1$ and $\mathbb{E}(1-\kappa_\tau)\sim2b\,\tau^2\log(1/\tau)$ for $a=1$. Consequently, for $p=n$ coordinates at the global scale $\tau_n=n^{-1/2}$, with $m_n$ the sum of the $1-\kappa_i$, $\mathbb{E}m_n\sim\frac{\pi}{B(a,b)\sin(\pi a)}n^{1-a}$ for $0<a<1$ and $\mathbb{E}m_n\sim b\log n$ for $a=1$.
results.label: mp:thm:effsize

results.name: Rates agree between effective model size and number of species
results.summary: The growth rates of the effective model size and of the expected number of blocks under the matching Poisson Dirichlet law are the same, and the constants differ by a factor between about 0.89 and 1.
results.statement: The rates in the effective model size theorem are exactly those of $\mathbb{E}K_n$, the expected number of blocks in a sample of size $n$, under $\mathrm{PD}(\alpha,\theta)$ with $(\alpha,\theta)=(1-a,\,a+b-1)$. The constants agree exactly when $a=1$, both being $b$, and for $a<1$ they differ by the factor $\Gamma(2-a)$, which lies in $[\Gamma(1.4616),1]\approx[0.8856,1]$ for every $a\in(0,1]$.
results.label: mp:cor:agree

results.name: The shrinkage count and the species count fluctuate differently
results.summary: The effective model size concentrates around its mean while the number of blocks under the Pitman Yor partition has a nondegenerate random limit.
results.statement: Fix $a\in(0,1)$ and $b>0$, let $\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_n$ be independent with the law of $\kappa_{\tau_n}$ at $\tau_n=n^{-1/2}$, put $m_n=\sum_{i=1}^n(1-\kappa_i)$, and let $K_n$ be the number of blocks in a sample of size $n$ from $\mathrm{PD}(\alpha,0)$ with $\alpha=1-a$. Then $m_n/\mathbb{E}m_n\to1$ in probability, with $\{\operatorname{Var}m_n\}^{1/2}/\mathbb{E}m_n\sim\frac{\sin(\pi a)}{\pi}\{B(a,2-a)B(a,b)\}^{1/2}n^{-(1-a)/2}$, whereas $K_n/n^{\alpha}\to M_\alpha$ almost surely, where $M_\alpha$ is Mittag Leffler with $\mathbb{E}M_\alpha^r=r!/\Gamma(1+r\alpha)$. The limit is nondegenerate, so the coefficient of variation of $K_n$ converges to $\{2\Gamma(1+\alpha)^2/\Gamma(1+2\alpha)-1\}^{1/2}$, equal to $0.7555$ at $\alpha=1/2$, while that of $m_n$ converges to zero.
results.label: mp:prop:fluct

results.name: Exchangeability forces the Ewens predictive weights
results.summary: If the one step forecast is affine in the empirical distribution and the sequence is exchangeable, the weights are theta over theta plus n and n over theta plus n.
results.statement: Let $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an exchangeable sequence, and suppose there are a diffuse (atomless) distribution function $H$ on $[0,1]$ with $X_1\sim H$ and constants $c_n\in(0,1)$ such that for every $n\ge1$, almost surely and for all $x$, $\mathbb{P}(X_{n+1}\le x\mid X_1,\dots,X_n)=c_nH(x)+(1-c_n)F_n(x)$, where $F_n$ is the empirical distribution function of $X_1,\dots,X_n$. Set $\theta=c_1/(1-c_1)\in(0,\infty)$. Then for every $n\ge1$, $c_n=\theta/(\theta+n)$ and $1-c_n=n/(\theta+n)$, so that $\mathbb{P}(X_{n+1}\in\cdot\mid X_1,\dots,X_n)=\frac{\theta}{\theta+n}H(\cdot)+\frac{1}{\theta+n}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{X_i}(\cdot)$.
results.label: esf:prop:weights

results.name: Exact finite n variance and a moment estimator of theta
results.summary: The variance of an empirical average under the Ewens predictive rule is exact for every n and can be inverted to give theta without any asymptotic approximation.
results.statement: Let $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ be exchangeable with $X_1\sim H$, $H$ a diffuse distribution function on $[0,1]$, and suppose that for constants $c_n\in(0,1)$ and every $n\ge1$, $\mathbb{P}(X_{n+1}\le x\mid X_1,\dots,X_n)=c_nH(x)+(1-c_n)F_n(x)$ almost surely for all $x$, where $F_n$ and $P_n$ are the empirical distribution function and the empirical measure of $X_1,\dots,X_n$; set $\theta=c_1/(1-c_1)$. Then for every $n\ge1$, every $g\in L^2(H)$ and every $x$, $\operatorname{Var}(\int g\,dP_n)=\operatorname{Var}_H(g)\frac{\theta+n}{n(1+\theta)}$ and $\operatorname{Var}(F_n(x))=H(x)(1-H(x))\frac{\theta+n}{n(1+\theta)}$. Consequently, with $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(\int g\,dP_n)$, $\theta=n(\operatorname{Var}_H(g)-v_n)/(nv_n-\operatorname{Var}_H(g))$.
results.label: esf:prop:exactvar

results.name: The de Finetti architecture is invariant under abundance weighting
results.summary: Weighting the sampling probabilities by a function of abundance keeps the sample exchangeable and changes only the mixing measure.
results.statement: Let $P=(p_1\ge p_2\ge\cdots)$ have the Poisson Dirichlet law with parameter $\theta>0$, let $\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots$ be independent draws from a diffuse distribution $H$, and let $w:(0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable with $0<\sum_\ell w(p_\ell)p_\ell<\infty$ almost surely. Given $P$ and $(\xi_\ell)$, let $X^w_1,X^w_2,\dots$ be independent with common law $\tilde P^w=\sum_\ell w(p_\ell)p_\ell\delta_{\xi_\ell}/\sum_\ell w(p_\ell)p_\ell$. Then $(X^w_i)$ is exchangeable, and its empirical distribution functions $F^w_n$ converge almost surely and uniformly to a random distribution function, the distribution function of $\tilde P^w$, whose law is the de Finetti measure of the sequence. Relative to the unweighted paintbox only the mixing measure changes.
results.label: esf:prop:invariant

results.name: The negative branch is not a weighted paintbox
results.summary: A two parameter partition law with negative discount cannot be reproduced by weighting a one parameter Poisson Dirichlet paintbox.
results.statement: Let $\alpha<0$ and $\theta=m|\alpha|$ with $m$ a positive integer, so that the two parameter paintbox with parameters $(\alpha,\theta)$ has frequencies $(P_1,\dots,P_m)\sim\mathrm{Dirichlet}(|\alpha|,\dots,|\alpha|)$ on $m$ types. For no $\theta'>0$ and no measurable $w:(0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ with $0<\sum_\ell w(p_\ell)p_\ell<\infty$ almost surely is the weighted paintbox built on Poisson Dirichlet frequencies $(p_\ell)$ with parameter $\theta'$, which samples atom $\ell$ with probability proportional to $w(p_\ell)p_\ell$, equal in law to the two parameter paintbox with parameters $(\alpha,\theta)$.
results.label: esf:prop:notweighted

results.name: Closure of the Ewens Pitman family under weighted sampling
results.summary: Sampling a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet population in the size biased layout with a power density keeps the Ewens Pitman family closed only in the Ewens case or when the density is uniform.
results.statement: Let $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$, with $0\le\sigma<1$ and $\theta>-\sigma$, be the two parameter Poisson Dirichlet (Ewens Pitman) law, lay its atoms on $(0,1)$ as the stick breaking subdivision in size biased order, and drop sample points with the density $f_\alpha(x)=\alpha(1-x)^{\alpha-1}$, $\alpha>0$, instead of uniformly. The induced law is again a member of the Ewens Pitman family if and only if $\sigma=0$ or $\alpha=1$.
results.label: py:thm:pitman

results.name: Rigidity of the residual allocation structure
results.summary: Among sampling densities that charge every interval, only power weights keep the induced subdivision of the size biased layout a residual allocation model, so for a discount strictly between zero and one no such density other than the uniform one carries a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet law to the stick breaking sequence of another member of the family.
results.statement: Let $G$ be continuous and strictly increasing with $G(0)=0$ and $G(1)=1$ (equivalently, the sampling density charges every interval), and lay the atoms in size biased order. Then the induced subdivision, read in the order in which its intervals are laid, is again a residual allocation model with independent factors if and only if $G(r)=r^{\alpha}$ for some $\alpha>0$. Consequently, for $\sigma\in(0,1)$ no such sampling density and direction makes the induced subdivision, in its layout order, the stick breaking sequence of another member of the Ewens Pitman family, apart from the uniform density.
results.label: py:thm:rigid

results.name: No Kingman type genealogy produces the two parameter family
results.summary: A genealogy in which the mutation probability depends only on the number of branches gives a count of types with variance at most its mean, which rules out positive discount.
results.statement: Consider any genealogical rule in which, with $j$ branches present, the defining event is a mutation with probability $p_j\in[0,1]$ and a binary coalescence otherwise, with $p_j$ depending only on $j$. Then the number of types satisfies $K_n=\sum_{j=1}^n\xi_j$ with $\xi_j\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_j)$ independent, so $\operatorname{Var}[K_n]\le\mathbb{E}[K_n]$. No such rule produces $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$ with $\sigma>0$, for which $\operatorname{Var}[K_n]\asymp n^{2\sigma}\gg\mathbb{E}[K_n]\asymp n^{\sigma}$.
results.label: py:prop:nocoal

results.name: Exponent map of the number of types under power sampling
results.summary: Sampling a Poisson Dirichlet population in the size biased layout with a power density gives an exact power law envelope and moves the growth exponent of the number of types from sigma to sigma star.
results.statement: Let $0<\sigma<1$, lay the $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$ atoms in size biased order, and sample with the density $f_\alpha(x)=\alpha(1-x)^{\alpha-1}$, $\alpha>0$. Let $\widetilde R_k=\prod_{i\le k}(1-B_i)$ be the residual after $k$ stick breaking factors and $K_n$ the number of types in a sample of size $n$. Then almost surely $\widetilde R_k\,k^{(1-\sigma)/\sigma}\to M\in(0,\infty)$ and $\log K_n/\log n\to\sigma_*=\sigma/\{\alpha(1-\sigma)+\sigma\}$.
results.label: py:prop:pyimage

results.name: The sigma diversity is a power of the stick envelope
results.summary: The almost sure limit of the number of types over n to the sigma equals the sigma th power of the stick envelope constant over sigma, with no constant left over.
results.statement: Let $0<\sigma<1$ and $\theta>-\sigma$, let $S$ be the almost sure limit of $K_n/n^{\sigma}$ under $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$ (the $\sigma$ diversity), and let $M=\lim_k\widetilde R_kk^{(1-\sigma)/\sigma}$ be the limit of the scaled stick residuals in size biased order, where $\widetilde R_k=\prod_{i\le k}(1-B_i)$ and $B_i$ are the stick breaking fractions. Then $S=(M/\sigma)^{\sigma}$ almost surely.
results.label: py:lem:MS

results.name: The weighted diversity is a power of the unweighted diversity
results.summary: Under power sampling the limit of the number of types over n to the sigma star is a constant times a power of the unweighted sigma diversity.
results.statement: Let $0<\sigma<1$ and $\theta>-\sigma$, lay the $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$ atoms in size biased order and sample with the density $f_\alpha(x)=\alpha(1-x)^{\alpha-1}$, $\alpha>0$ (the weighted paintbox), with $\sigma_*=\sigma/\{\alpha(1-\sigma)+\sigma\}$. Let $S_*$ be the almost sure limit of $K_nn^{-\sigma_*}$ and $S$ the almost sure limit of $K_nn^{-\sigma}$ under the unweighted $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$. Then $S_*=C\,S^{\kappa}$ almost surely, with $\kappa=\alpha\sigma_*/\sigma=\alpha/\{\alpha(1-\sigma)+\sigma\}$, for a constant $C=C(\sigma,\alpha)$.
results.label: py:prop:power

results.name: The constant in the diversity power law
results.summary: The constant relating the weighted and unweighted diversities has a closed form in gamma functions, does not depend on theta, and equals one for uniform sampling.
results.statement: In the identity $S_*=C\,S^{\kappa}$ between the weighted and unweighted diversities of $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$ under sampling with the density $f_\alpha(x)=\alpha(1-x)^{\alpha-1}$ in size biased order, with $0<\sigma<1$, $\alpha>0$ and $\sigma_*=\sigma/\{\alpha(1-\sigma)+\sigma\}$, the constant is $C=\alpha^{\sigma_*}\sigma^{(\alpha-1)\sigma_*}\,\Gamma(1-\sigma_*)\Gamma(1-\sigma+\sigma_*)/\Gamma(1-\sigma)$. In particular $C$ does not depend on $\theta$, and $C=1$ at $\alpha=1$.
results.label: py:prop:constant

results.name: Bias of the singleton fraction
results.summary: Under an exact power law envelope with exponent sigma star, the expected singleton fraction exceeds sigma star by a relative amount of one over twice the expected number of types.
results.statement: Suppose the induced frequencies follow the envelope $p_k=c\,k^{-1/\sigma_*}$ exactly, and write $A=nc$. Then as $A\to\infty$, $\mathbb{E}[A_1\mid P]=\sigma_*\Gamma(1-\sigma_*)A^{\sigma_*}+O(A^{-\delta})$ and $\mathbb{E}[K_n\mid P]=\Gamma(1-\sigma_*)A^{\sigma_*}-\tfrac12+O(A^{-\delta})$ for some $\delta>0$, where $A_1$ is the number of singletons, and consequently $\mathbb{E}[A_1\mid P]/\mathbb{E}[K_n\mid P]=\sigma_*\big(1+\frac{1}{2\mathbb{E}[K_n\mid P]}\big)+o\big(1/\mathbb{E}[K_n\mid P]\big)$.
results.label: py:prop:rate

results.name: Growth regimes of the number of types under weighted sampling
results.summary: For a discount strictly between zero and one, the growth of the number of types under a general sampling weight is classified by the behaviour of the weight at the origin, from bounded through a power of log n and a power of n to n divided by a slowly varying function.
results.statement: Lay the $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\theta)$ atoms in either layout, $0<\sigma<1$, and sample with a weight whose distribution function $G$ is continuous and increasing. (i) If $G$ is slowly varying with a density $g$ near the origin such that $rg(r)$ is slowly varying, then $\sigma_*=1$ and $K_n=n/L(n)$ for a slowly varying $L$. (ii) If $G$ is regularly varying with index $\rho\in(0,\infty)$, with a density near the origin regularly varying with index $\rho-1$, then $K_n=n^{\sigma_*}L(n)$ with $\sigma_*=\sigma/\{\rho(1-\sigma)+\sigma\}$. (iii) If $G(r)=\exp\{-r^{-\tau}(1+o(1))\}$ for some $\tau>0$, then $K_n=(\log n)^{\sigma/\{\tau(1-\sigma)\}}L(\log n)$ for a slowly varying $L$. (iv) If $G\equiv0$ on $(0,r_0)$ for some $r_0>0$, then $K_n$ is bounded almost surely.
results.label: py:thm:regimes

results.name: Inverse gamma series for PIG(0)
results.summary: The Polya Inverse Gamma variable that turns a reciprocal gamma factor into a Gaussian kernel is an explicit series of independent inverse gamma variables, with finite mean and infinite variance.
results.statement: Let $Y_1,Y_2,\dots$ be independent inverse gamma variables with shape $3/2$ and scale $1$, that is $1/Y_k\sim\mathrm{Ga}(3/2,1)$. Then $X_0=\sum_{k\ge1}Y_k/(4k^2)$ converges almost surely and satisfies $\mathbb{E}[e^{-s^2X_0}]=e^{-\gamma s}/\Gamma(1+s)$ for $s>0$, with $\gamma$ the Euler Mascheroni constant. In particular $\mathbb{E}[X_0]=\sum_k1/(2k^2)=\zeta(2)/2=\pi^2/12$, while $\operatorname{Var}(X_0)=\infty$.
results.label: pig:prop:pig0

results.name: Good's rule is the Ewens predictive
results.summary: Under the Ewens model, Good's predictive probability for a species seen r times is r over n plus theta, and the unseen mass is theta over n plus theta.
results.statement: Under the Ewens sampling formula with parameter $\theta$ and sample size $n$, with $a_r(n)$ the number of species seen exactly $r$ times, $\mathbb{E}[a_r(n)]=\frac{\theta}{r}\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\frac{\Gamma(\theta+n-r)}{\Gamma(\theta+n)}$ for $1\le r\le n$. Consequently Good's estimator of the population frequency $q_r$ of a species seen $r$ times, $\mathbb{E}[q_r\mid\text{data}]=\frac{r+1}{n+1}\frac{\mu_{r+1,n+1}}{\mu_{r,n}}$ with $\mu_{r,n}=\mathbb{E}[a_r(n)]$, equals $r/(n+\theta)$ for $r\ge1$, with unseen mass $q_0=\theta/(n+\theta)$, the probability that the next specimen is a new species.
results.label: pig:prop:good

results.name: Predictive law of the number of new species
results.summary: The number of new species in m further specimens is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables given theta, with explicit mean and variance in terms of the digamma function.
results.statement: Under the Ewens sampling formula, let $U_m$ be the number of new species among $m$ further specimens after $n$ have been seen. Then given $\theta$, $U_m$ has the law of $\sum_{i=n}^{n+m-1}B_i$ with independent $B_i\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\theta/(\theta+i))$, independent of the first $n$ specimens, so $\mathbb{E}[U_m\mid\theta]=\theta[\psi(\theta+n+m)-\psi(\theta+n)]$ and $\operatorname{Var}[U_m\mid\theta]=\sum_{i=n}^{n+m-1}\theta i/(\theta+i)^2$, where $\psi$ is the digamma function.
results.label: pig:prop:newspecies

results.name: Asymptotic redundancy of the Bayes estimator of theta
results.summary: For the Ewens richness likelihood, the posterior of the log concentration is asymptotically normal, and the Bayes estimator and credible interval agree with the maximum likelihood estimator and Wald interval to leading order.
results.statement: Let $K$ be the number of species in a sample of $n$ specimens under the Ewens sampling formula with parameter $\theta$, let $\varphi=\log\theta$, let $\hat\theta$ and $\hat\varphi=\log\hat\theta$ be the maximum likelihood estimates, let $J_n=\operatorname{Var}(K\mid\hat\theta)$ be the observed information in $\varphi$, and let $I(\theta)=\operatorname{Var}(K\mid\theta)/\theta^2$ be the Fisher information in $\theta$. For any prior with a continuous positive density at $\hat\theta$, the posterior of $\varphi$ is asymptotically $N(\hat\varphi,J_n^{-1})$ as $J_n\to\infty$. The posterior mean satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid K]=\hat\theta+O(\hat\theta J_n^{-1})$, the central $95\%$ credible interval equals the Wald interval $\hat\theta\pm1.96\,I(\hat\theta)^{-1/2}$ up to $o(\hat\theta J_n^{-1/2})$, and two priors differing by a smooth reweighting give posteriors within total variation $O(J_n^{-1/2})$ and posterior means within $O(\hat\theta J_n^{-1})$.
results.label: pig:prop:bvm

results.name: Tail of the concentration posterior
results.summary: Under a gamma type prior with no exponential decay, the posterior of theta has a Pareto tail, so its moments exist only when the number of species is small enough.
results.statement: Let $K$ be the number of species in a sample of $n$ specimens under the Ewens sampling formula with parameter $\theta$. Under the prior $\pi(\theta)\propto\theta^{a_0-1}e^{-b_0\theta}$ with $a_0>0$, $b_0\ge0$, the posterior $p(\theta\mid K)\propto\theta^{K+a_0-1}e^{-b_0\theta}\Gamma(\theta)/\Gamma(\theta+n)$ has right tail $p(\theta\mid K)\sim c\,\theta^{K+a_0-1-n}e^{-b_0\theta}$ as $\theta\to\infty$. If $b_0>0$ the tail is light and every posterior moment is finite. If $b_0=0$ the tail is Pareto of index $n-K-a_0$: the posterior is proper if and only if $K+a_0<n$, and $\mathbb{E}[\theta^p\mid K]<\infty$ if and only if $p<n-K-a_0$. Under the flat prior $(a_0,b_0)=(1,0)$ the posterior is proper if and only if $K\le n-2$, has finite mean if and only if $K\le n-3$, and finite variance if and only if $K\le n-4$.
results.label: pig:prop:tail

results.name: Residue formula for the normalizing constant of a rational density
results.summary: The integral of a rational function with poles of any multiplicity in the cut plane is a finite sum of residues times logarithms and powers.
results.statement: Let $R=P/Q$ be rational with poles at $-r_1,\dots,-r_J$ of multiplicities $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_J$, where $r_i\in\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$, and write the Laurent coefficients $\gamma_{ij}=\frac{1}{(\mu_i-j)!}\frac{d^{\mu_i-j}}{d\alpha^{\mu_i-j}}\{(\alpha+r_i)^{\mu_i}R(\alpha)\}|_{\alpha=-r_i}$, so that $R(\alpha)=\Pi(\alpha)+\sum_i\sum_{j=1}^{\mu_i}\gamma_{ij}/(\alpha+r_i)^j$ with $\Pi$ the polynomial part. If $\deg Q\ge\deg P+2$ then $\Pi\equiv0$, $\sum_i\gamma_{i1}=0$, and $\int_0^\infty R(\alpha)\,d\alpha=-\sum_i\gamma_{i1}\log r_i+\sum_i\sum_{j=2}^{\mu_i}\gamma_{ij}/((j-1)r_i^{\,j-1})$, with the principal logarithm.
results.label: rc:thm:residue

results.name: Mellin transform of a Pochhammer density
results.summary: The Mellin transform of a Pochhammer density has a closed form on its maximal strip, which gives fractional and negative moments and the expected log.
results.statement: Let $[x]^k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$ denote the rising factorial, let $a,c>0$ and let $m,d,b$ be nonnegative integers with $b\ge m+d+1$. Let $R(\alpha)=\alpha^d[\alpha]^m/[c\alpha+a]^b$, with simple poles at $-r_i$, $r_i=(a+i-1)/c$, and partial fraction expansion $R(\alpha)=\sum_{i=1}^b\gamma_i/(c\alpha+a+i-1)$. On the strip $-\{d+\mathbf{1}(m\ge1)\}<\operatorname{Re}(s)<b-m-d$ the Mellin transform is $\mathcal{M}(s)=\int_0^\infty\alpha^{s-1}R(\alpha)\,d\alpha=\frac{\pi}{c\sin(\pi s)}\sum_{i=1}^b\gamma_ir_i^{\,s-1}$. When $b\ge m+d+2$ the strip contains $s=1$, and then the normalizing constant is $C=\mathcal{M}(1)=-c^{-1}\sum_i\gamma_i\log r_i$, $\mathbb{E}(\alpha^{s-1})=\mathcal{M}(s)/\mathcal{M}(1)$ for the law with density proportional to $R$, and $\mathbb{E}(\log\alpha)=\sum_i\gamma_i\log^2r_i/(2\sum_i\gamma_i\log r_i)$.
results.label: rc:thm:mellin

results.name: Shrinkage rate of the half horseshoe, corrected
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Wang and Polson (2024), Pochhammer priors for sparse count models, arXiv:2402.09583.
results.summary: Every Pochhammer prior attains the Kullback Leibler rate N^{-1} log N, and the half horseshoe only gives the smaller constant, which corrects the reading of the earlier bound.
results.supersedes: The reading of Proposition 2 of Wang and Polson (2024) under which the choice $m=0$ is needed for the Kullback Leibler superefficient rate $N^{-1}\log N$.
results.label: rc:cor:rate

results.name: Exact tail index of the Pochhammer law
results.summary: The Pochhammer density is regularly varying with an exact tail index given by its parameters, so it has power law tails and finitely many moments.
results.statement: Let $[x]^k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$, let $a,c>0$, let $m,d,b$ be nonnegative integers with $b\ge m+d+2$, and let $\alpha$ have the density $p(\alpha)=\alpha^d[\alpha]^m/\{C[c\alpha+a]^b\}$ on $\alpha>0$, with $C$ the normalizing constant. Then $\mathbb{P}(\alpha>x)\sim x^{-(b-m-d-1)}/\{C\,c^b\,(b-m-d-1)\}$ as $x\to\infty$, so the law is regularly varying with index $b-m-d-1$ and has exactly $b-m-d-2$ finite moments. The half horseshoe $m=0$, $b=2$, $d=0$ has index one and no moments.
results.label: rc:cor:tail

results.name: Conditional exponentiality of the half horseshoe
results.summary: A Pochhammer density is completely monotone exactly when m and d are zero, in which case it is a scale mixture of exponentials, which yields an exact latent variable sampler.
results.statement: Let $[x]^k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$, let $a,c>0$, let $m,d,b$ be nonnegative integers with $b\ge m+d+2$, and let $R(\alpha)=\alpha^d[\alpha]^m/[c\alpha+a]^b$, with poles $-r_i$, $r_i=(a+i-1)/c$, and partial fraction expansion $R(\alpha)=\sum_{i=1}^b\gamma_i/(c\alpha+a+i-1)$. Then $R$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$ if and only if $m=d=0$. In that case $R(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty e^{-\alpha\tau}g(\tau)\,d\tau$ with $g(\tau)=c^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^b\gamma_ie^{-r_i\tau}\ge0$, which is proportional to the density of $T=E_1+\dots+E_b$ with $E_i$ independent exponential with rate $r_i$; equivalently $\alpha\mid\tau\sim\mathrm{Exp}(\tau)$ with $p(\tau)=C^{-1}g(\tau)/\tau$, and the normalizing constant is $C=\int_0^\infty\tau^{-1}g(\tau)\,d\tau=-c^{-1}\sum_i\gamma_i\log r_i$.
results.label: rc:thm:cm

results.name: Tilted normalizer with exponential integrals
results.summary: Exponentially tilting a rational density gives a normalizer that is a finite sum of exponential integrals, valid for every degree of the numerator.
results.statement: Let $\lambda=-\log z>0$, let $P$ be a polynomial and write $P(\alpha)/[c\alpha+a]^b=\Pi(\alpha)+\sum_{i=1}^b\gamma_i/(c\alpha+a+i-1)$ with $\Pi(\alpha)=\sum_k\pi_k\alpha^k$ and poles $-r_i$, $r_i=(a+i-1)/c$. Then $\int_0^\infty z^{\alpha}P(\alpha)/[c\alpha+a]^b\,d\alpha=\sum_kk!\,\pi_k/\lambda^{k+1}+c^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^b\gamma_ie^{\lambda r_i}E_1(\lambda r_i)$, where $E_1(x)=\int_x^\infty t^{-1}e^{-t}\,dt$. No degree condition is required, and all moments exist.
results.label: rc:thm:tilt

results.name: Exact dispersion block for Negative Binomial regression
results.summary: The dispersion parameter of Negative Binomial regression with a Pochhammer prior has an exact conditional law, so a partially collapsed Gibbs sampler needs no Metropolis step.
results.statement: Let $n_i$, $i=1,\dots,K$, be Negative Binomial counts with dispersion $\alpha$ and success probabilities $\pi_i=e^{\psi_i}/(1+e^{\psi_i})$, where $\psi_i$ is the linear predictor in the regression coefficients $\beta$, so that $p(n_i\mid\alpha,\beta)=\frac{[\alpha]^{n_i}}{n_i!}\frac{(e^{\psi_i})^{n_i}}{(1+e^{\psi_i})^{n_i+\alpha}}$ with $[\alpha]^k=\alpha(\alpha+1)\cdots(\alpha+k-1)$. Marginally in the Polya Gamma augmentation variables $\omega$, $p(\alpha\mid n,\beta)\propto\prod_{i=1}^K[\alpha]^{n_i}\,z^{\alpha}\,p(\alpha)$ with $z=\prod_{i=1}^K(1+e^{\psi_i})^{-1}$. Hence, with a Pochhammer prior $p(\alpha)\propto[\alpha]^m/[c\alpha+a]^b$ and any integer $b\ge0$ and $a,c>0$, the conditional law of $\alpha$ is exactly the tilted Pochhammer law with numerator $[\alpha]^m\prod_i[\alpha]^{n_i}$, tilt $z$ and $\lambda=\sum_i\log(1+e^{\psi_i})=-\log z$, and drawing $\alpha$ from it before redrawing $\omega$ gives a partially collapsed Gibbs sampler with the correct stationary distribution.
results.label: rc:prop:dispersion

results.name: Zipf tails of the Negative Binomial Beta Pochhammer hierarchy
results.summary: The marginal law of the counts in the hierarchy has an exact power law tail with a logarithmic correction, so a Zipf exponent can be set as a prior hyperparameter.
results.statement: Let $[x]^k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$, and let $\alpha$ have the normalized density $p_\alpha(\alpha)\propto[\alpha]^m/[c\alpha+a]^b$ on $\alpha>0$, with $m,b$ nonnegative integers, $b\ge m+2$ and $a,c>0$, let $\pi\mid\alpha\sim\mathrm{Beta}(c\alpha+a,b)$ and $n\mid\alpha,\pi\sim\mathrm{NB}(\alpha,\pi)$. Then as $n\to\infty$, $p(n)\sim K\,n^{-(1+a)}(\log n)^{-(1+\iota)}$ with $\iota=1+\mathbf{1}(m\ge1)$ and $K=\Gamma(a)\Gamma(1+\iota)\varpi/(B(a,b)c^{1+\iota})$, where $\varpi=\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\alpha^{-\mathbf{1}(m\ge1)}p_\alpha(\alpha)$.
results.label: rc:thm:zipf

results.name: Boundary Zipf law of the Yule Simon prior predictive
results.summary: Under a Pochhammer prior on the Zipf exponent the Yule Simon prior predictive is proper but has no positive moments.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ have the normalized density $p_\rho(\rho)\propto1/[c\rho+a]^b$ on $\rho>0$, with $b\ge2$ an integer, $a,c>0$ and $[x]^b=x(x+1)\cdots(x+b-1)$. The Yule Simon prior predictive, $p(n)=\int\rho B(n,\rho+1)p_\rho(\rho)\,d\rho$, satisfies $p(n)\sim p_\rho(0)\,n^{-1}(\log n)^{-2}$ as $n\to\infty$. This is a proper distribution, since $\sum_nn^{-1}(\log n)^{-2}<\infty$, but it has no moments of any positive order.
results.label: rc:prop:boundaryzipf

results.name: The check loss identifies the posterior
results.summary: Minimizing the expected check loss over maps of a uniform variable and the data recovers the posterior quantile function exactly.
results.statement: Let $\mathbb{E}|\theta|<\infty$ and suppose that for $P$ almost every $y$ the conditional distribution function $F_y$ of $\theta$ given $Y=y$ is continuous and strictly increasing on the interior of its support. Then $H^\star=\arg\min_H\mathbb{E}_{(\theta,Y)}\mathbb{E}_{U\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)}\rho_U(\theta-H(U,Y))$, with $\rho_u$ the check loss, over measurable $H$ exists, is unique up to sets of measure zero in $(u,y)$, and satisfies $H^\star(u,y)=F_y^{-1}(u)$.
results.label: suff:thm:check

results.name: A bottleneck that attains the Bayes risk is sufficient
results.summary: If a learned map that factors through a summary of the data attains the minimal check loss, the summary is sufficient, so sufficiency can be tested by comparing risks.
results.statement: Let $(\theta,Y)$ have a joint law with $\theta$ real, prior $\pi$ and $\mathbb{E}|\theta|<\infty$, let $P$ be the marginal law of $Y$, and suppose that for $P$ almost every $y$ the conditional distribution function $F_y$ of $\theta$ given $Y=y$ is continuous and strictly increasing on the interior of its support. Let $\rho_u(z)=z\{u-\mathbf{1}(z<0)\}$ be the check loss, $\mathcal{R}(H)=\mathbb{E}_{(\theta,Y)}\mathbb{E}_{U\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)}\rho_U(\theta-H(U,Y))$, and $\mathcal{R}^\star$ its minimum over measurable $H$. Suppose $H(u,y)=g(u,T(y))$ for some measurable $g$ and $T$, and $\mathcal{R}(H)=\mathcal{R}^\star$. Then $T$ is Bayes sufficient for $\theta$, that is, the conditional law of $\theta$ given $Y=y$ equals its conditional law given $T(Y)=T(y)$ for $P$ almost every $y$. If moreover the data space is countable, as it is for allelic partitions and site frequency spectra, then $T$ is sufficient in the Fisher Neyman sense for the family $\{p(\cdot\mid\theta):\theta\in\Theta_0\}$ for a set $\Theta_0$ of prior probability one; and if in addition the prior has full support and $\theta\mapsto p(y\mid\theta)$ is continuous for every $y$, then $T$ is sufficient for the whole family.
results.label: suff:thm:suff

results.name: Excess risk is a posterior distance
results.summary: The extra check loss of a summary based map is sandwiched between multiples of the expected squared Wasserstein distance between the posterior and its summary based version.
results.statement: Let $H(u,y)=g(u,T(y))$ with $u\mapsto g(u,T(y))$ nondecreasing, and write $\pi_T(\cdot\mid y)$ for the law with quantile function $u\mapsto g(u,T(y))$. Suppose that for $P$ almost every $y$ the posterior has a density $f_y$, and that there are constants $0\le\underline\delta\le\bar\delta<\infty$ such that for almost every $(u,y)$ the inequality $\underline\delta\le f_y\le\bar\delta$ holds on the closed interval with endpoints $F_y^{-1}(u)$ and $g(u,T(y))$. Then $\frac{\underline\delta}{2}\mathbb{E}_YW_2^2(\pi(\cdot\mid Y),\pi_T(\cdot\mid Y))\le\mathcal{R}(H)-\mathcal{R}^\star\le\frac{\bar\delta}{2}\mathbb{E}_YW_2^2(\pi(\cdot\mid Y),\pi_T(\cdot\mid Y))$, where $W_2$ is the 2 Wasserstein distance on the line.
results.label: suff:thm:quant

results.name: Converse of the bottleneck sufficiency theorem
results.summary: A Bayes sufficient statistic always admits a map through it that attains the minimal risk.
results.statement: If $T:\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is Bayes sufficient for $\theta$ then there exists a measurable $g:(0,1)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\Theta$ with $\mathcal{R}(g(\cdot,T(\cdot)))=\mathcal{R}^\star$.
results.label: suff:prop:converse

results.name: The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta
results.summary: Given a single segregating site, the chance that it is carried by n minus 1 sequences changes with theta, so the count of sites is not sufficient.
results.statement: Consider $n$ sequences under Kingman's coalescent with infinite sites mutation at scaled rate $\theta$ and known ancestral states. Let $\ell_i$ be the total length of branches subtending exactly $i$ leaves, $L=\sum_i\ell_i$ the total tree length, $\xi_i$ the number of sites whose derived allele is carried by exactly $i$ sequences, $S=\sum_i\xi_i$ the number of segregating sites, $a_n=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^{-1}$ and $b_n=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^{-2}$. Conditionally on the tree the $\xi_i$ are independent $\mathrm{Poisson}(\theta\ell_i/2)$, so $S\sim\mathrm{Poisson}(\theta L/2)$ and $\xi\mid S,\text{tree}\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(S;\ell/L)$, free of $\theta$. Unconditionally, let $e_{n-1}$ be the spectrum with a single site carried by $n-1$ sequences and $\phi_n(\theta)=\mathbb{P}(\xi=e_{n-1}\mid S=1,\theta)=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{n-1}e^{-\theta L/2}]/\mathbb{E}[Le^{-\theta L/2}]$. Then for $n\ge3$, $\phi_n(0+)=1/\{(n-1)a_n\}$ and $\phi_n'(0+)=-(a_n-b_n)/\{(n-1)a_n^2\}<0$. In particular $\phi_n$ is not constant in $\theta$, and $S$ is not sufficient for $\theta$.
results.label: suff:prop:notsuff

results.name: Bernoulli geometric duality between the Ewens block count and segregating sites
results.summary: The number of blocks of the Ewens sampling formula has the same law as one plus the number of coalescent levels that carry at least one mutation.
results.statement: Let $S_2,\dots,S_n$ be independent with $\mathbb{P}(S_k=j)=p_k(1-p_k)^j$ for $j\ge0$ and $p_k=(k-1)/(k-1+\theta)$, the numbers of mutations on a genealogy drawn from Kingman's coalescent while $k$ ancestral lineages remain under infinite sites mutation at rate $\theta/2$. Then $K_n\overset{d}{=}1+\#\{k\in\{2,\dots,n\}:S_k\ge1\}$, where $K_n$ is the number of blocks under the Ewens sampling formula with the same $\theta$.
results.label: coal:cor:duality

results.name: The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta, likelihood argument
results.summary: The conditional law of the infinite sites data given the site count depends on theta through the latent tree, shown explicitly for three and four sequences.
results.statement: Under Kingman's coalescent with infinite sites mutation at rate $\theta/2$, let $X$ denote the full infinite sites data on $n$ sequences, $S(X)$ its number of segregating sites, $G$ the genealogy and $L_G$ its total length. Then $p(X\mid\theta)=(\theta/2)^{S(X)}\int e^{-\theta L_G/2}w(X,G)\,\mu(dG)$, where $w$ and the genealogy law $\mu$ are free of $\theta$. The conditional law of $X$ given $S$ depends on $\theta$ unless the measures $w(X,G)\mu(dG)$, pushed forward to $L_G$, are proportional across configurations with equal $S$. For $n=3$ and $n=4$ they are not, so $S$ is not sufficient for $\theta$.
results.label: coal:prop:notsuff

results.name: DeepSets encoders factor through the site frequency spectrum
results.summary: Any encoder built from per site permutation invariant features depends on the data only through the site frequency spectrum, which caps what such an encoder can learn.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the $n\times S$ binary matrix of infinite sites data with columns $x_1,\dots,x_S$, one per segregating site, and call an encoder of per site DeepSets form if $e(X)=\rho\big(\sum_{j=1}^S\phi(x_j)\big)$ with $\phi$ invariant under permutation of the $n$ lineages. Every such encoder satisfies $e(X)=\rho\big(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\xi_i\,\tilde\phi(i)\big)$ for some $\tilde\phi$, where $\xi_i$ is the number of sites at which exactly $i$ of the $n$ sequences carry the derived allele, and is therefore a function of the site frequency spectrum $\xi$ alone.
results.label: coal:thm:deepsets

results.name: The spectrum is a strict coarsening of the gene tree
results.summary: The site frequency spectrum is strictly coarser than the gene tree, which is the maximal invariant, so no per site DeepSets encoder can recover what the spectrum loses.
results.statement: Under the infinite sites model without recombination, the maximal invariant of the data matrix $X$ under relabelling of lineages and permutation of sites is the gene tree, that is, the unlabelled rooted topology with mutation counts on its edges. The site frequency spectrum $\xi$ is a strict coarsening of it, already at $n=4$ sequences with two segregating sites. Consequently no per site DeepSets encoder, at any depth or width, can recover the information in $X$ that is not already in $\xi$.
results.label: coal:cor:coarse

results.name: The haplotype count escapes the site frequency spectrum
results.summary: The haplotype count is invariant under relabelling of lineages and sites but is not a function of the site frequency spectrum.
results.statement: The haplotype count $H=H(X)$, the number of distinct rows of the infinite sites data matrix $X$, is invariant under relabelling of lineages and under permutation of sites, and $H$ is not a function of the site frequency spectrum $\xi$.
results.label: coal:prop:hap

results.name: Conjecture, rigidity of Poisson Dirichlet under general ascertainment
results.summary: No sampling weight depending on atom index and position that charges every interval is conjectured to carry a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet law to a different one.
results.statement: Let $0<\sigma<1$ and $\vartheta>-\sigma$. There is no sampling weight, depending measurably on the atom index and the atom's position in the subdivision and charging every interval, that carries $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma,\vartheta)$ to $\mathrm{PD}(\sigma',\vartheta')$ for any $(\sigma',\vartheta')\ne(\sigma,\vartheta)$.
results.label: future:conj:rigid
